subject: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request

Team — quick ask on a high-impact EAP for PrimeBank (Enterprise, strategic). They have a binding go-live condition in their procurement that requires us to provide deterministic model snapshots and an export window for their auditors plus a one-time export of inference logs for the onboarding audit. Without this, legal will withhold final signature (deal PB-2026-0473).

I attached the spec they supplied (primebank_eap_spec_v1.pdf) and a rough cost/effort estimate (redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx). Key asks from the customer thread are:
- Deterministic model freeze (ability to pin exact model weights/quantization and ensure identical outputs for a given prompt set)
- Secure export window for one-time logs + periodic snapshot exports (S3-compatible encrypted bundle)
- Audit-friendly retention + checksum verification

Business ask: can Product/Eng triage and let us know by EOD Tue (2026-09-14) whether this is possible in the next two sprints or if we need to offer the dedicated-instance workaround (routing PrimeBank to a dedicated residency with export support) as the only go-live path?

Tradeoffs are understood — performance/latency, storage, and long-term maintenance. If we can scope an MVP (minimal deterministic freeze + one export) that can land in ~4 weeks, sales can commit to a partial contract signature and push for an accelerated take in Q4.

Proposed next steps:
1) Product to confirm scope and gating criteria (what 'deterministic' means operationally).
2) Eng to provide a high-level effort estimate and blockers.
3) If no faster path, confirm whether we can allocate a dedicated instance as stopgap and what the net cost is.

Thanks — attaching spec & estimate. This is a time-sensitive procurement condition.

— Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request

Thanks Laura — important ask. A few clarifying questions before Eng sizes:
- Does PrimeBank require cryptographic hash verification of the model weights (to prove immutability), or is an API-level pinned-version enough?
- For the export window: are they asking for a one-off export for onboarding plus scheduled exports, or a single one-time export only?

From a product perspective, the "deterministic freeze" needs a clear acceptance test: a prompt set + seed + KV cache state that we can replay and get identical token streams. That implies capturing tokenizer/version, quantization parameters, and exact kernel selection. If they want a cryptographic artifact bundle, that raises compliance + storage questions.

Jasmine — can you list the primary engineering dependencies (KV cache snapshot, model artifact immutability, export pipeline encryption) and a ballpark effort? If we can decompose into an MVP that only supports: (A) pin model build+quantization for inference, (B) one-time export of last-30-days logs with encryption, that might be doable faster.

If Engineering needs >2 sprints, we should prepare the dedicated-instance fallback and price it into commercial terms.

Rishi
Director, Product Management

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request

On Mon, Sep 14, 2026 at 08:43 AM Rishi M wrote:
> From a product perspective, the "deterministic freeze" needs a clear acceptance test...

Quick technical readout — keeping it high level:
Primary engineering pieces and rough complexity:
- Model artifact immutability: medium. We already have build provenance; adding an exportable signed bundle (weights + quant params + tokenizer hash) is ~2 dev-weeks + 1 security review.
- Deterministic replay acceptance test: medium-high. We need a small harness to capture RNG seeds, KV cache snapshot, and a deterministic inference runner for replay across releases — ~3-4 dev-weeks.
- Export pipeline for logs/snapshots (encrypted S3 bundle with checksums): low-medium if leveraging existing export infra — ~2 dev-weeks plus infra tasks for encrypted transient storage.
- Operational gating: canaries, can rollbacks, and retention policies — ~1 dev-week for policies + config UI work if Product needs an admin knob.

So conservative timeline for an MVP (pin build + one-time export + replay harness) is ~6 weeks of focused work (approx 3 sprints) given current capacity. If we prioritize it into the next sprint (force-off other items) we might compress to ~4 weeks but that needs exec sign-off.

Workarounds:
- Dedicated instance path: stand up a pinned model on a dedicated pool for PrimeBank and expose an export API. Pros: fastest (2 weeks) and operationally simple; cons: higher recurring cost and more manual work for us.
- Hybrid: deliver the signed artifact export first (2-3 weeks) while we build the replay harness in parallel. That could satisfy procurement if they accept artifact + planned replay timeline.

I've attached a preliminary effort breakdown (redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx) referenced by Laura. If Product can confirm acceptance criteria (exact hashes vs pinned-version), we'll finalize a Jira ticket and scope the sprints.

Jasmine Liu
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>, Liam O'Connor <pmc-contracts@primebank.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request

Looping to push for prioritization — this is a near-term revenue milestone (PB-2026-0473). Commercial notes: PrimeBank has signaled they will split signature (60% now) if we can commit to the artifact export + a defined delivery plan for the replay harness. They've asked for a decision by COB Thu (2026-09-16).

Options for Product/Eng decision:
1) Commit to MVP roadmap (artifact export + one-time logs export) in 4 weeks, with replay harness in subsequent sprint. We market this as a two-phase delivery.
2) Approve dedicated-instance fallback (2 weeks) and price it into the deal — gets them live quickly but increases TCO and complicates scale precedent.
3) Decline and ask Sales to renegotiate procurement terms (risk: deal stalls).

If Product/Eng can sign option (1) or (2) by Thu COB, I'll update PrimeBank legal and push the partial signature through. I'm prepared to shift two sprint slots (swap with a lower-priority internal item) to accelerate.

Requested ask: Product (Rishi) please confirm acceptance criteria (hash vs pinned artifact) and Jasmine please confirm if you can target the compressed path (4 weeks) if we reallocate sprint capacity.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
